newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT RATIFIES TREATY WITH HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT RATIFIES TREATY WITH HUNGARY.

text.p: Romania's parliament on Thursday ratified a recently signed friendship treaty with Hungary, which is expected to help the two former Warsaw pact members join NATO and the European Union.
Members of the 341-strong lower Chamber of Deputies voted by 159 to one, with 27 abstentions, to ratify the long-delayed "understanding, cooperation and good neighbourhood" treaty.
Parliament's upper house, the Senate, endorsed the treaty last week.
The treaty is the "first such document signed by Romania in time of peace, liberty, sovereignity and independence," Bucharest radio said.
The pact, agreed under Western pressure, settles old border rifts and provides guarantees for the rights of the 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians in Romania's central Transylvania region.
The treaty is seen as a major step for the two countries' ambitions to join NATO and the EU.

MPs of both the nationalist Romanian National Party (PUNR) and the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR), a party representing the interests of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians, have refused to vote on Thursday, the state radio said.
"The ambiguity of some articles in the treaty can harm Romania's national sovereignity," PUNR deputy Costica Ciurtin said.
"The wording of the treaty does not meet the (Hungarian) minority's expectations," Bucharest radio quoted a UDMR parliamentarian as saying.

The accord, signed by Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his Romanian counterpart Nicolae Vacaroiu in the western city of Timisoara on September 16, has yet to be promulgated by Romanian President Ion Iliescu. REUTER
